entityDescription:
The Centro Studi Demetra (Development of European Mediterranean Transportation) is the Association born in 2006 by the commitment of exponents of the academic, entrepreneurial and institutional world with the aim to encourage, in Italy, initiatives regarding formative, legal, administrative and economic aspects in the transport sector, with particular regards to the civil aviation.
The experience matured in these first four years of activity has run the Association to elaborate on the new frontier of the community politic in the innovation technology and ecologic sector, main themes of great interest and in continuous evolution. These themes have to be analyzed with particular attention to the security and have to be matched with the evolution of others sectors as the aerospace and the microlight.
Demetra establishes oneself as authoritative cultural reference of the civil aviation environment, that extends from the microlight to the space, achieving important recognitions, among which, the actual audition within the cognitive investigation on the Italian airport system conducted by the transports, mails and telecommunications Committee of the Chamber of the deputies.
The Centro Studi Demetra performs specialist popularization activities and, for this goal, it organizes conferences, seminars and lectures tense to promote the debate on the aerial transport politic, creating occasions of comparison among the political and academic referents, the maximum institutional authorities, the entrepreneurial vertexes, the most accredited experts to deepen, in particular, the problems of the sector connected to the consequential transformations derived by the liberalization and privatization of the system and the relative adjustment of the community legislation rules. 
Besides, for several months now the Centro Studi Demetra entertains, near its head office in Rome, the meetings of the work plan on the "Regulation" that the Agusta Westland, with the collaboration of The European House Ambrosetti, has started, within the study on "The development of the aerial transport to vertical take-off in the context of a state-of-the-art mobility system for the Country", with the final purpose to define, in sight of the future EXPO 2015, the premises normative for a middle-long term plan of infrastructures and heliports able to allow the necessary development of the mobility through the means vertical take-off.
Within its activities, Demetra also occupy oneself with the education and the refresher training of its members representatives besides the meetings that are periodically held near its center.
The Demetra publishing project will lead to the publication of a "Aerial transport code¿, consistent in a selection of the national and community legislation, of extreme utility for the sector stakeholders they daily have to consult the numerous and various normative sources that discipline the aerial transport.

TISICS manufactures high performance light weight metal matrix composite components and net shape light alloys by diffusion bonding. TISICS manufactures silicon carbide monofilament use to reinforce aluminium or titanium alloys to increases tensile strength, stiffness, elevated temperature performance and to reduce thermal expansion. The metal composites have exceptional compressive strength exceeding the performance of steel. Reinforcement can be tailored to transition between materials with different mechanical performance.
TISICS lightweight metal composite have applications in struts, pressure vessels, actuators including robotic system components and structures with a typical 30% weight reduction. Components optimised for net shape hollow manufacture and load path aligned fibre reinforcement can achieve 70% mass reduction.
Titanium composites have strengths in excess of 1.6GPa, stiffness 210GPa and compression strengths above 2.5GPa. 
Aluminium composites tensile strength >1200MPa, Stiffness>140GPa Compression strength >1600MPa.

TISICS is developing net shape chemical propellant tanks and very thin wall COPV liners as well as metallic transition joint tubing for propulsion systems

TISICS is developing diaphragm materials compatible with a range of propellants
TISICS is a UK based SME with pilot scale facilities for development work and small batch manufacturing.

entityDescription: UHI North West and Hebrides is an institute of further and higher education which offers both full time and part time programmes. The three main college campuses are located in Thurso, Fort William and Stornoway with a number of smaller campuses around the region providing access for students and staff across a large geographical area. In addition a network of electronically linked learning centres allows UHI North West and Hebrides to reach learners in remote areas, meet the needs of employers, and support local economic activity and development. UHI North West and Hebrides is an academic partner of the University of the Highlands and Islands (UHI), a unique partnership of colleges and research institutions across the Highlands and Islands of Scotland. Each college and research institution has its own distinctive character and strengths. This means that students of UHI can share in the educational advantages of a larger institution whilst benefiting from the personal attention which a smaller college, like UHI North West and Hebrides, can provide. UHI North West and Hebrides hosts three prestigious research centres - the Environmental Research Institute (Thurso) and the UHI Centre for History (Dornoch) and the Centre for Recreation and Tourism (Fort William). All centres support the educational and economic development of the area, with research focussed on contemporary environmental and societal issues, and the role of heritage tourism. entityDescription:
The University of Nova Gorica is an institution of higher education that provides undergraduate and graduate study programs and conducts scientific research.

It started in 1995 as the School of Environmental Sciences, the first international graduate school in Slovenia, founded by the Municipality of Nova Gorica and the Jozef Stefan Institute of Ljubljana. Due to the introduction of new study programs and the expansion of scientific research activities, the School was reorganized in 1998 and renamed Nova Gorica Polytechnic. In 2006 the institution changed its status and became the University of Nova Gorica. Its founders are the Municipality of Nova Gorica, the Municipality of Ajdovscina and Jozef Stefan Institute from Ljubljana. 

Today the University of Nova Gorica provides education at seven schools: School of Science, School of Environmental Sciences, School of Engineering and Management, School of Humanities, School of Viticulture and Enology, School of Arts, and the Graduate School, which offers the following doctoral study programs: Environmental Sciences, Physics, Karstology, Comparative Studies of Ideas and Cultures, Linguistics, Molecular Genetics and Biotechnology and Economics and Techniques for the Conservation of the Architectural and Environmental Heritage.

Research is conducted at twelve laboratories and centers (Center for Astrophysics and Cosmology, Laboratory for organic matter physics, Laboratory for multiphase processes, Laboratory for Environmental Research, Materials research laboratory, Laboratory for quantum optics, Center for Atmospheric Research, Center for Biomedical Sciences and Engineering, Center for Cognitive Science of Language, Center for Systems and Information Technologies, Research Center for Humanities and Wine Research Center.
